prop:knot-operator-lp-selection:
Proposition Knot operators are selected per confinement by the LP/SDP dual basis of the Frobenius Gram pseudo-inverse. Let R be the categorical coefficient ring with q \in R generic, and let \{b_i\} be the normal-form basis of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q). The data of the statement are:

  • a finite family \mathcal{O} of knot operators o = T_{m,m'}, each carrying a braid word \beta(o) \in B_n, which acts in H_n(q) through \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i;
  • a cost t_o \in R for each operator o \in \mathcal{O};
  • a confinement target T \in H_n(q) with normal form \mathrm{NF}(T) = \sum_i c_i \, b_i.

From these data define:

  • the Frobenius Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \, b_j) and its Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse G^{+}, the inverse of the trace form on the quotient H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad} by its radical; when G is non-degenerate, G^{+} = G^{-1};
  • the supply matrix S, whose column o is the coefficient vector of \beta(o) in the normal-form basis, S_{i,o} = [b_i]\,\mathrm{NF}(\beta(o));
  • the demand vector n_T, with n_T^{i} = \max(0, -c_i), the magnitudes of the negative normal-form coefficients of T.

The selection of knot operators producing T is the linear program

  \min_{\substack{x \in R^{\mathcal{O}},\; x \geq 0 \\ G^{+} S x \;\geq\; n_T}}
  \;\;\sum_{o \in \mathcal{O}} t_o \, x_o .

Given a primal optimum and a dual optimum with equal objective values (strong duality, assumed here), complementary slackness holds, and the LP dual variables y^* \geq 0 supply the shadow prices of the demand constraints and the active set \{o : x_o^* > 0\} identifying which knot operators contribute to the bound state. A target with no negative normal-form coefficient has n_T = 0 and is met by the empty selection x = 0.

The statement holds for every choice of the family \mathcal{O}, its braid words and the cost t; these enter only through S and the objective. The LP is feasible if and only if n_T is dominated componentwise by some non-negative combination of the columns of G^{+} S. The dual solution isolates the minimum-cost generators.

Operator family and cost. The instance used in this paper takes n = 3 and the family

  \mathcal{O} = \{T_{1,0},\, T_{2,3},\, T_{2,5},\, T_{2,7},\, T_{2,9},\, T_{3,4},\, T_{3,5}\},

the unknot together with the torus knots embeddable in the genus-4 fibre. Each torus knot T_{m,m'} carries its standard torus braid (\sigma_0 \cdots \sigma_{m-2})^{m'} \in B_m, and B_2 \subset B_3 through \sigma_0 \mapsto \sigma_0, so that \beta(T_{1,0}) = 1, \beta(T_{2,m'}) = \sigma_0^{m'} and \beta(T_{3,m'}) = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^{m'} in H_3(q). The cost of an operator is the crossing energy of its braid word, t_o = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\beta(o)): each positive crossing contributes q and each negative crossing -q^{-1}. Every word above is a positive braid with (m-1)m' crossings, so t_{T_{m,m'}} = (m-1)\,m'\,q and t_{T_{1,0}} = 0.
sec:plancherel-knot-factor-mass-tower-pr:
Equipped with the Plancherel measure and the ribbon writhe derivation, the per-link knot factor K(\beta) can be evaluated in closed form across the principal topological families of the particle and nuclear spectrum.

This section derives the spectral knot factor for amphicheiral knots (such as the figure-eight 4_1), three-component Borromean composites, and shell-closed torus configurations. It formulates the Pauli exclusion factor via Wedderburn projection onto antisymmetric column hooks, stratifies the mass-tower expansion coefficients by cellular depth, and connects the flavor-dressing functor and the staircase electroweak residual (\sin^2\theta_W) to the S_4 \downarrow S_3 half-symmetric branching projection.
prop:knot-factor-spectral-form:
Proposition Knot factor a_K as a central Gram pairing. Let \mathcal{K} be a knot with braid representative \beta_\mathcal{K} \in B_n and mirror \beta_\mathcal{K}^*. Work in the semisimple Hecke algebra A = H_n(R, q) with central idempotents \{e_\lambda\}_{\lambda \vdash n}, irreducible characters \chi_\lambda, and d_\lambda := \chi_\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = \dim V_\lambda. Let \tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda be the Markov trace, normalised by \tau(\mathbf{1}) = 1, and let

  \pi(x) \;:=\; \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n} \frac{\chi_\lambda(x)}{d_\lambda}\, e_\lambda

be the projection of A onto its centre. Define the knot factor as the Gram pairing of the central part of \beta_\mathcal{K} with its mirror,

  a_\mathcal{K} \;:=\; \frac{\tau\bigl(\pi(\beta_\mathcal{K})\, \beta_\mathcal{K}^*\bigr)}{\tau(\mathbf{1})}.

Then

  a_\mathcal{K}
  \;=\;
  \tau\bigl(\pi(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\pi(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    w_\lambda \,
    \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})\, \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)}
         {d_\lambda^{\,2}},
  \qquad
  w_\lambda \;:=\; \tau(e_\lambda) \;=\; y_\lambda\, d_\lambda ,

and the weights satisfy \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1. Taking \beta_\mathcal{K} = \mathbf{1} gives a_\mathbf{1} = 1. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), w_\lambda = 0 for every \lambda with three or more rows, so only the two-row blocks contribute. The identity holds exactly in R.
prf:knot-factor-spectral-form:
Proof Proof of knot factor spectral derivation. The e_\lambda are orthogonal central idempotents, so e_\lambda x = x e_\lambda and \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x) = \delta_{\lambda\mu}\,\chi_\lambda(x) for every x \in A. Hence

  \tau(e_\lambda x) \;=\; \sum_\mu y_\mu\, \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x) \;=\; y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda(x).

With x = \mathbf{1} this gives w_\lambda = \tau(e_\lambda) = y_\lambda d_\lambda, and \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = \tau\bigl(\sum_\lambda e_\lambda\bigr) = \tau(\mathbf{1}) = 1. With x = \beta_\mathcal{K}^* and linearity of \tau,

  \tau\bigl(\pi(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\beta_\mathcal{K}^*\bigr)
  \;=\; \sum_\lambda \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})}{d_\lambda}\, y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)
  \;=\; \sum_\lambda w_\lambda\, \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*)}{d_\lambda^{\,2}}.

Since \chi_\lambda(\pi(x)) = \chi_\lambda(x), the same computation with \pi(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) in place of \beta_\mathcal{K}^* gives the same sum. For \beta_\mathcal{K} = \mathbf{1} every ratio is 1 and the sum is \sum_\lambda w_\lambda = 1. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), y_\lambda = 0 for three-row \lambda, so w_\lambda = 0 there. \square

Scope. The projection \pi is essential. The uncentred entry \tau(\beta_\mathcal{K}\,\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) equals \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}\beta_\mathcal{K}^*), the character of a product, which is not the product of characters unless one factor is central. Weighting that uncentred entry by \dim_q^2 V_\lambda / [n]_q! would at \beta_\mathcal{K} = \mathbf{1} require 1 = \sum_\lambda \dim_q^2 V_\lambda/[n]_q!, which fails for q \neq 1.
cor:knot-factor-amphicheiral:
Corollary Knot factor for Markov-amphicheiral knots: sum of positive squares. Let \mathcal{K} be Markov-amphicheiral. Its mirror braid representative \beta_\mathcal{K}^* is conjugate to \beta_\mathcal{K} in H_n(R, q). There exists w \in H_n(R, q)^{\times} such that:

  \beta_\mathcal{K}^* \;=\; w\,\beta_\mathcal{K}\, w^{-1}.

The knot factor is therefore a sum of positive squares weighted by Plancherel weights:

  a_\mathcal{K} \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash n}\, w_\lambda\,
  \frac{\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})^2}{\chi_\lambda(\mathbf{1})^2}.
prf:knot-factor-amphicheiral:
Proof Proof of knot factor amphicheiral. By trace cyclicity, \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) = \chi_\lambda(w\,\beta_\mathcal{K}\, w^{-1}) = \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}) for every \lambda. Substituting in (knot factor) a_\mathcal{K} = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) / \chi_\lambda(\mathbf{1})^2 yields the displayed expression. \square

Worked example (\mathcal{K} = 4_1 in B_3). Take the figure-eight braid \beta_{4_1} = \sigma_1\,\sigma_2^{-1}\,\sigma_1\,\sigma_2^{-1}. Direct computation of the Hoefsmit characters on the three partitions \lambda \vdash 3 at the aether q_0 gives:

\lambda \chi_\lambda(\beta_{4_1}) \chi_\lambda(\beta_{4_1}^*) match?
(3) +1 +1 yes
(2,1) -1 -1 yes
(1,1,1) +1 +1 yes

All three characters agree, so \beta_{4_1}^* is conjugate to \beta_{4_1} in H_3(q) — i.e. 4_1 is Markov-amphicheiral. The displayed formula therefore applies, with

  a_{4_1} \;=\;
  w_{(3)}\cdot 1
  \;+\; w_{(2,1)}\cdot \tfrac{1}{4}
  \;+\; w_{(1,1,1)}\cdot 1.

This is the alternating-block projection used in the {}^3\mathrm{H} and {}^3\mathrm{He} formulas — not a fitted ansatz.
cor:knot-factor-borromean-composite:
Corollary Borromean-k composite knot factor is a = (1 - h^2)^k. Consider a Brunnian k-component composite, where every (k{-}1)-component sublink is trivial. Suppose its central-idempotent expansion decouples: the composite knot factor is the product of the components' factors, with no cross-term,

  a_{\mathrm{Bor}_k} \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{k} a_i .

Then if the components share a common factor a_i = a for all i, the composite knot factor is a^k. In particular, with each component at the figure-eight pairing a_{4_1} = 1 - h^2,

  a_{\mathrm{Bor}_k} \;=\; (1 - h^2)^k .

Decoupling is the Brunnian content; the k-th power is what the product becomes under uniformity, and the two are stated separately because only the first is a hypothesis about the link.

The per-component value is a hypothesis here, not an import. Knot factor for Markov-amphicheiral knots: sum of positive squares derives, under the block normalisation it states, a_K = 1 - w_{\mathrm{alt}}(1 + h^2) rather than the displayed 1 - h^2; that block records the difference as a normalisation question about the non-alternating blocks, not as a rearrangement. The two agree exactly when w_{\mathrm{alt}}(1 + h^2) = h^2, and at w_{\mathrm{alt}} = 0 every component is 1, so the composite is 1 for every h and every k and the corollary constrains h not at all.

prop:pauli-factor-wedderburn:
Proposition Pauli factor F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} is the alt/sym Wedderburn-block trace ratio. Working over A = H_n(R, q), the Pauli statistical weight in nuclear Q-value formulas is the ratio of Wedderburn-block traces:

  F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}(\beta_\mathcal{K})
  \;=\;
  \frac{\int_{A_{(1^n)}}\!\rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})}
       {\int_{A_{(n)}}\!\rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\chi_{(1^n)}(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \cdot \dim_q V_{(1^n)}}
       {\chi_{(n)}(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \cdot \dim_q V_{(n)}}
  \,\in\, R.

This is the alternating-block trace divided by the symmetric-block trace. Both blocks are one-dimensional, with \sigma_i \mapsto q on V_{(n)} and \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1} on V_{(1^n)}, so for a braid of writhe (exponent sum) w

  \frac{\chi_{(1^n)}(\beta_\mathcal{K})}{\chi_{(n)}(\beta_\mathcal{K})}
  \;=\; (-1)^{w}\, q^{-2w}.

This is a unit of R for every braid and depends only on the writhe. It never vanishes, so it does not detect bosonic or fermionic content of \beta_\mathcal{K}.

def:flavor-dressing-functor:
Definition Flavor dressing functor. The flavor dressing functor assigns a dressed-mass scale to each quark flavor:

  \mu \colon \mathbf{Flavor} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0},
  \qquad
  q \in \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}, \mathfrak{c}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{t}\}
  \longmapsto
  \mu_q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}.

The discrete category \mathbf{Flavor} contains the six quark flavors and identity morphisms. The target \mathbb{R}_{>0} is the positive real line with canonical commutative-monoid structure under multiplication.

The focus is the doublet \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}\}. Heavy flavors are included for forward compatibility, with their individual \mu_q values open.

The functor bridges two categorical layers:

  1. Aether side. The splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is determined by the aether flavor split modulo the pair-skein factor.
  2. Bounds side. The splitting respects the categorical bound enforced by the aether factors \hbar_q, h_q, and [2]_q.

The flavor dressing functor composes with the shell dressing morphism at the hadron and atom levels:

\begin{tikzcd}
  \mathbf{Flavor}
  \arrow[r, "\mu"] \arrow[d, "\Phi"]
  & \mathbb{R}_{>0}
  \\
  \mathbf{Hadron}
  \arrow[r, "m_{\mathrm{bare}}"']
  & \mathbb{R}_{>0}
  \arrow[u, "P_{\mathrm{bare}} \mapsto P_{\mathrm{dressed}}"']
\end{tikzcd}

Here \Phi is the quark-content functor. The right-vertical arrow lifts a bare hadron mass to its electron-dressed atomic mass.

The discrete-category framing ensures compatibility with other categorical constructions. Sums over flavors in hadronic mass formulas become natural transformations of functors rather than ad-hoc weighted sums.

prop:flavor-dressed-mass-from-aether-spl:
Proposition Aether-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting. Conditional on the aether flavor split conjecture.

Let \mu \colon \mathbf{Flavor} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} be the flavor dressing functor. Let m_{\mathfrak{p}}, m_{\mathfrak{n}} be the nucleon masses, M_N = (m_{\mathfrak{p}} + m_{\mathfrak{n}})/2, and q > 1 the aether parameter. The down-up dressed mass splitting is exactly determined by the aether flavor formula:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;=\;
  M_N \cdot \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \cdot
  \frac{q\,(q^{2} + 1)}{q^{4} + 1}
  \;+\;
  O\!\left(\bigl(\Delta m / M_N\bigr)^2\right).

Dropping the O correction yields the leading-order aether-pure form:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;\approx\;
  \frac{M_N}{3} \cdot
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q \cdot
  \frac{1}{\kappa},
  \qquad
  \kappa = \frac{q^4 + 1}{q\,(q^2 + 1)}.

The CODATA neutron-proton mass difference is no longer an input. The functor extracts the splitting purely from q_0 and the scale M_N. The individual masses \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} and \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} are then pinned by the baryon-content sum-rule.

Here \kappa = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}) at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the sum of the two crossing weights of the pair Skein formula. It satisfies q\,\kappa = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma^2), the Hopf-link trace, and 1/\kappa \le 1 for q > 0.

What is assumed and what is derived. Two inputs are assumed. The first is the aether flavor split conjecture, read at leading order as the equality m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} = M_N (q-1)^2(1-q^{-4})/3. The second is the nucleon form of the pair Skein mass formula, (m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}})\,q(q^2 + 1) = (q^4 + 1)(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}). This form is derived from the pair Skein formula when the proton and neutron masses are the sums of their pair masses (nucleon map). The O\!\left((\Delta m / M_N)^2\right) correction is absorbed in these inputs. From them the leading-order splitting follows by dividing by q^4 + 1 > 0 and substituting. The conjecture is not proved. The leading-order equality is the strongest reading of the conjecture, and the CODATA comparison records that it is not met exactly at physical values, so the proposition is a statement about the model under that reading.
thm:flavor-mass-splitting-bound:
Theorem Two-sided aether bound on the dressed-quark splitting. Conditional on the aether flavor split conjecture. The closed form for \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is derived from that conjecture and the nucleon form of the pair Skein mass formula, with M_N = (m_{\mathfrak{p}} + m_{\mathfrak{n}})/2.

For aether parameter q > 1, the down-up splitting satisfies the two-sided bound:

  0 \;<\; \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;\le\; \tfrac13\, M_N \cdot \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
  \;<\; M_N \cdot \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q,

where \hbar_q = (q - 1)/q, h_q = q - q^{-1}, and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.

The bound is on the difference rather than the individual masses, which isolates the aether-derivable quantity from the CODATA-anchored mean.
prf:flavor-mass-splitting-bound:
Proof Proof of flavor mass splitting bound. Sketch.

Two ingredients:

  1. Positivity (lower bound). By aether construction, q > 1 implies (q-1)^2 > 0 and 1 - q^{-4} > 0. Their product is positive; division by 3 preserves the sign. By Aether-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting the splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is M_N times this positive aether factor (modulo O((\Delta m / M_N)^2), which is below the leading term), so the difference is strictly positive.

  2. Upper bound. The aether factor satisfies

    \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
    \;<\;
    \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^2} \cdot (q - q^{-1}) \cdot (q + q^{-1})
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2 (q^4 - 1)}{q^4}.

Both expressions share the numerator (q-1)^2; their ratio is

    \frac{(1 - q^{-4}) / 3}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q^4 - 1)/(3 q^4)}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{1}{3},

The aether factor of the proposition equals 1/3 of the bound expression times the convention-D Skein factor q(q^2+1)/(q^4+1). That factor is at most 1 for q > 0, because

    q^4 + 1 - q(q^2 + 1) = (q - 1)(q^3 - 1) \;\ge\; 0 .

So the splitting is at most \tfrac13 M_N \hbar_q^2 h_q [2]_q, which is strictly below M_N \hbar_q^2 h_q [2]_q. \square

Tightness

The bound is not tight: the slack-ratio identity above shows that the realised splitting is exactly (1/3) \cdot q(q^2+1)/(q^4+1) of the bound (plus a small higher-order correction); at q_0 this is 0.328. The sharper bound factor q(q^2+1)/(q^4+1) equals 1 only at q = 1. The dominant factor is the explicit 1/3 baked into the aether formula of Aether-pure derivation of the u--d flavor split. Tightening would require either:

  • A finer aether factor that absorbs the 1/3 directly into the categorical derivation (rather than as an artefact of the closed-form algebra).
  • A different categorical bound source (e.g. Hecke convergence bound: \mathrm{MAE}(H_k) \leq C \cdot r^{-(k-3)} applied to the splitting word) — but this requires further development and is not committed in this revision.

Per-flavor bounds (out of scope)

This theorem does not assert per-flavor bounds 0 < \mu_q < c \cdot M_N. Such bounds require additional non-aether inputs (the nucleon-baryon sum rule for the average \bar\mu) and live in the open follow-up; see Dressed-quark numerology at q_0.

prf:y-lambda-closed-form-wenzl-bridge:
Proof Proof of y lambda closed form wenzl bridge. By [Wenzl 1988] (cited in [Orellana, math/9806163, Theorem on p.17]), the unique Markov trace on the type-A Iwahori-Hecke algebra in g-convention with parameter z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r (1 - Q)/(1 - Q^r) has weights \omega_\lambda(Q) = s_{\lambda, r}(Q) given by the principal-specialization Schur function. By [Chlouveraki HDR Theorem 6.20 (=Juyumaya Theorem 12, d=1 case)], the type-A Markov-trace family is 1-dimensional, parameterised by z.

The convention isomorphism g = q\sigma transports \mathrm{tr}_M on \sigma-Hecke (with the \sigma-convention z) to \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{GL}} on g-Hecke (with z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q z). Both traces have the same expansion \mathrm{tr} = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda for any choice of irreducible character basis (which is intrinsic to the algebra, hence convention-independent). By uniqueness, the weights agree:

  y_\lambda^{(\sigma)} \;=\; y_\lambda^{(g)} \;=\;
  \omega_\lambda(Q) / Z, \qquad Z := \sum_\mu d_\mu \omega_\mu(Q),

normalised so \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1. \square

Specialisation at z = q^3/(q^2+1)

At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), so z_{\mathrm{GL}} = qz = Q^2/(1+Q) with Q = q^2, and the defining equation z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r(1-Q)/(1-Q^r) has the exact solution r = 2. The specialisation is then s_\lambda(1, Q) — a Schur polynomial in two variables — which vanishes identically for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3 and, on the two-row stratum \lambda = (n-k,k), equals

  s_{(n-k,k)}(1, Q) \;=\; Q^k \bigl(1 + Q + \cdots + Q^{\,n-2k}\bigr)
  \;=\; q^{\,n}\,[\,n-2k+1\,]_q .

The q^n cancels against the normaliser Z, leaving y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^n and y_\lambda = 0 for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3. So the row cap is not an extra hypothesis: it is r = 2, the dimension of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fibre, read off the bridge equation itself.

Per-partition agreement at H_3, H_4, H_5 (representative entries):

See Table 2.

The two legs are the principal-specialisation route above and the q-integer closed form; they agree identically, not to a numerical tolerance, and \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 holds exactly at each n.

No independent numerical cross-check of the bridge at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is recorded here.

prop:chi-lambda-w0-sign-weighting:
Proposition Long-element \chi_\lambda(w_0) sign-character weighting of the c_k chain at H_3. Let \mathcal{B}_n and \mathcal{B}_p be canonical nucleon braids. The empirical coefficients c_k^{(\lambda)} do not match a uniform Plancherel-weighted sum. Instead, they require weighting by the character values at the longest element w_0 \in S_3:

  S_k^{(w_0)} \;:=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3}
    \chi_\lambda(w_0) \cdot c_k^{(\lambda)}
  \;=\; c_k^{(3)} \;-\; c_k^{(1,1,1)}.

The longest element w_0 plays the role of central reversal. The c_k Markov-trace decomposition is thus governed by the maximal mixing element, not the identity.
prf:chi-lambda-w0-sign-weighting:
Proof Proof of chi lambda w0 sign weighting. Step 1 — character values at w_0. The longest element w_0 \in S_3 is the involution (1\,3) (cycle type [2,1]). Standard S_n character theory gives:

  • \chi_{(3)}(w_0) = 1: trivial rep is constant.
  • \chi_{(2,1)}(w_0) = 0: the standard 2-d rep maps the transposition (1\,3) to a reflection; trace of a reflection in 2-d is 0.
  • \chi_{(1,1,1)}(w_0) = -1: sign rep gives \mathrm{sgn}(w_0) = -1 (odd permutation).

Step 2 — per-irrep closed forms at H_3(q). By All three V_\lambda per-irrep character difference closed forms with cyclotomic factor pattern, the three character-difference closed forms are

\begin{aligned}
  \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)     &= -\tfrac{(q^2+1)^2(q^2-1)}{4q}, \\[4pt]
  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) &= -\tfrac{(q^4+1)(q^2-1)}{4q^3}, \\[4pt]
  \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) &= -\tfrac{(q^2+1)^2(q^2-1)}{4q^5}.
\end{aligned}

Step 3 — conjugate-partition symmetry. The conjugate-partition relation \chi_{(1,1,1)}\text{-diff}(q) = \chi_{(3)}\text{-diff}(q) / q^4 proved in All three V_\lambda per-irrep character difference closed forms with cyclotomic factor pattern, implies, expanding both at q = 1 + \varepsilon, that every \varepsilon^m coefficient (odd and even alike) of the V_{(1,1,1)} difference is a q^{-4} = (1+\varepsilon)^{-4} binomial-shift of the V_{(3)} coefficients:

  [\varepsilon^m]\,\chi_{(1,1,1)}\text{-diff}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{j = 0}^{m} (-1)^j \binom{j + 3}{j}\,
  [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)}\text{-diff}.

The indices j run over both parities. The c_k in this proposition's statement are the even-power coefficients c_k^{(\lambda)} = [\varepsilon^{2k}]\,\chi_\lambda\text{-diff}; restoring the full ε-expansion is needed to pick out the [\varepsilon^{2k}] contribution of \chi_{(1,1,1)}, which involves [\varepsilon^{2k - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} for j ranging over \{0, 1, \ldots, 2k\} — including odd values like j = 2k - 1 where the input is the odd-power coefficient [\varepsilon^1]\,\chi_{(3)}.

For m = 2k \geq 10 (i.e. k \geq 5), the binomial coefficient \binom{j+3}{j} grows monotonically in j, so the dominant contributions come from the largest j values where the [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} factor is still non-zero — the smallest non-trivial [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} sit at m - j \in \{1, 2\} per the witness data (e.g. [\varepsilon^1]\,\chi_{(3)} = -2, [\varepsilon^2]\,\chi_{(3)} = -3). At m = 10 the dominant contributions are therefore at j \in \{8, 9\}, where \binom{11}{8} = 165 and \binom{12}{9} = 220. The alternating sign (-1)^j from the (1+\varepsilon)^{-4} expansion combined with the consistently negative low-order \chi_{(3)} coefficients gives c_k^{(1,1,1)} \gg c_k^{(3)} in magnitude with sign tied to the parity of the dominant j.

Step 4 — sign-character coincidence. Substituting into S_k^{(w_0)} = c_k^{(3)} - c_k^{(1,1,1)} and observing that c_k^{(1,1,1)} \gg c_k^{(3)} for k \geq 5 (because of the q^{-4} amplification of the high-order ε-tail),

  \mathrm{sgn}\bigl(S_k^{(w_0)}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathrm{sgn}\bigl(-c_k^{(1,1,1)}\bigr)
  \;=\; -\mathrm{sgn}\bigl(c_k^{(1,1,1)}\bigr).

The empirical c_k from the Wenzl-bridge Markov trace at H_3 selects the same signed combination (canonical structural verification at k = 5, 6 above; the Markov-trace decomposition by Wenzl ([Wenzl 1988, Theorem 5]) factors through the character ring of S_3, with the long-element coefficient governing the sign-character extraction).

The sign agreement at k = 5, 6 is therefore the leading manifestation of the long-element character extraction in the c_k chain. \square

Open: magnitude closure

The proposition closes the sign at k = 5, 6. The magnitude ratios (1.49\times at c_5, 95.3\times at c_6) remain open. Candidate refinements:

  1. Cross-block coupling via \sigma_1 matrix elements. The V_{(2,1)} Hoefsmit matrix mixes the std rep into the diagonal sum at the b-element (off-diagonal Hoefsmit entry). The empirical c_k may carry a b^{2k}-multiplicative factor not captured by the diagonal \chi_\lambda values.
  2. q-deformed long-element character \chi_\lambda^q(w_0) at q = q_0 rather than q = 1. The character ring of H_3(q) differs from that of S_3 at q \neq 1; the appropriate weighting may use the q-deformed evaluation.
  3. Higher partitions (k \ge 7) where additional \lambda \vdash 3 cancellations or new \lambda \vdash 6 contributions enter via the Wenzl-bridge inductive ascent.

These extensions are flagged for follow-up under the closed-form resummation of the categorical stratum prefactors \alpha_k proposal.

rem:antiquark-channel-ledger:
Remark The antiquark ledger: why the meson channel is absent from step 2. Step 2 of the derived atom disposes of the antiquarks in six words — "either annihilate or form antinucleons" — and the nucleon-from-photons summary carries them through its conservation table as "3 quarks + 3 antiquarks" before keeping only the quarks. A third channel is available and is not named: three q\bar q pairs can bind as three mesons. This remark closes that gap, and the closure is not "the channel was overlooked" but "the channel carries zero binding on the framework's own formula".

The competition is between two channels, not three. Three pairs give three quarks and three antiquarks. Conserving baryon number, lepton number and charge, the exhaustive partitions are:

Channel Products Constituent knot \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}
A nucleon + antinucleon Borromean rings L6a4, twice 8G \approx 7.328 each
B three mesons L_+, three times 0 each
C annihilation back to \gamma\gamma — —

Channel C is the corpus's "annihilate"; channel A is its "form antinucleons". Channel B is the one step 2 omits.

Why A is selected, on the framework's own terms. The categorical mass invariant gives the physical binding energy as B(\mathfrak{H}) = m_\mathfrak{e}\cdot M(\mathfrak{H})|_{q = q_0}, and the hyperbolic volume of the constituent knot is what carries the geometric normalisation — torus knots contribute zero, hyperbolic knots contribute \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. The Borromean rings of channel A are hyperbolic; the Hopf link of channel B is a solid-torus complement with \mathrm{Vol} = 0. So channel A has strictly positive binding and channel B has none. A minimum-action selection between them is not close.

This is the same mechanism that makes m_\pi a calibration. Channel B's vanishing and the pion's missing mass scale are one fact seen twice: the meson sits below the hyperbolic threshold of the (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^n ladder, so the volume route reaches neither its mass nor its binding. The omission in step 2 is therefore justified — but for a reason the text does not give, and the reason is worth having, because it also predicts where the argument would fail. Were the meson's binding topology hyperbolic, channel B would compete and the derived atom would not follow.

What this does not say. Mesons are bound; the framework does not claim otherwise. The categorical meson records the Hopf-link binding raising the net normal-form amplitude by \approx 0.097 over the bare T_{01}\cdot T_{10} pair, and replacing that pair's neutrino component. So there is binding in the Hecke normal form and none in the volume normalisation, and the two are not in contradiction — they measure different things. What follows is only that B(\mathfrak{H}), as defined, does not reach channel B, which is exactly why m_\pi enters as CAL-3 rather than as a derivation.

A caution about the net. The three channels cannot be ranked by the normal-form net amplitude, even though all three are elements of the same H_3(q) at the same q_0. Binding raises the net: \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx +1.515 against the unbound pair's +1.418, while \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}) \approx +0.999. If minimum action meant minimum net, the bare pair would beat the bound meson and no meson would form. The minimised functional is the confinement SDP's optimal dual objective — the \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} of the mass invariant — and the net is not a proxy for it.
conj:kashaev-density-equals-sdp-multipli:
Conjecture Kashaev density prefactor equals joint-tower SDP Wedderburn multiplicity (\rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}). (Conditional.) Under the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture applied to an atomic Hecke element T_w with Markov closure knot/link K_w, the multiplicative density prefactor \rho_F \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} in the binding-energy formula

  B_{\mathrm{pred}}(K_w)
  \;=\;
  \rho_F \cdot m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(K_w)

equals the joint-tower SDP Wedderburn multiplicity \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w) of the canonical Hecke element T_w's saturating SDP solution in the H_{n}(q) Wedderburn decomposition:

  \rho_F  \;=\;  \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w)

per atom-knot-mass-derivation §Algorithm step 3 (the joint-tower SDP solve that produces \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} as a non-negative integer multiplicity).

Evidence (two confirmed atoms)

The identity is exact on the SDP-confirmed hyperbolic atoms (per atom-knot-mass-derivation line 265):

Atom K_w \rho_F (legacy) \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}
{}^{3}\mathrm{H} (T) knot 8_{11} 2 2
{}^{3}\mathrm{He} link L_{6a4} 2 2

The deuterium row that once headed this table has been removed, and the removal is not bookkeeping. It read {}^{2}\mathrm{H} \mid 6_2 \mid 1 \mid 1, assigning the deuteron the census knot 6_2 with \mathrm{Vol} \approx 4.40. The canonical deuteron knot is the braid closure (trefoil / Hopf), with \mathrm{Vol} = 0; the 6_2 assignment is retired, and the deuteron binding is not a hyperbolic-volume term. Since the identity's own formula is B_{\mathrm{pred}}(K) = \rho_F \, \mathfrak{m}_e \, \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(K), at \mathrm{Vol} = 0 it returns B_{\mathrm{pred}} = 0 for every value of \rho_F — so that row could not constrain the prefactor even in principle. It was not a stale entry contributing weak support; it was contributing none.

The evidence base for the \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} pattern is therefore two points, both equal to 2, not three points reading 1, 2, 2. The 1 was the row now removed, so the variation in that pattern came entirely from it.

Read this together with an operational finding: six operational definitions of \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} were computed and none reproduces the legacy triple, and the committed values carry the methodology tag "manual-historical-volume-match" — they are hand-assigned rather than derived.

The {}^{4}\mathrm{He} case uses the magic A \cdot 8G closure rule rather than a census knot. A binding-arbiter probe against AME2020 does not confirm an integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(⁴\mathrm{He}): the data-pinned prefactor is \rho_F(⁴\mathrm{He}) = B_{\mathrm{AME}}/(m_e A\,8G) \approx 1.889, which sits strictly between the isospin count (2T{+}1 = 1, T{=}0) and the monotone Wedderburn count (A{-}1 = \mathrm{sc}(3A) = 3). No clean categorical integer count reproduces 1.889; rounding it to 2 has no derived origin. Consequently the identity \rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} is scoped to the census-knot / linear-chain atoms ({}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{3}\mathrm{He}), where \rho_F = A{-}1 is exact and the SDP framing is canonical. At the doubly-magic point the prefactor is an empirical effective binding coefficient (\approx 1.89, Coulomb-corrected \approx 1.94), not an integer categorical multiplicity.

Categorical home

This identity is of the MacMahon-style partition-algebra type. The Wedderburn multiplicity of T_w's SDP solution is a partition-algebra count: it is the dimension of the saturating projection in the irreducible-block decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda). The agreement with the Kashaev density factor identifies \rho_F as such a count.

The published MacMahon-type statement about the colored Jones function is the Garoufalidis--Loebl formula. With \mathrm{Ferm}(A) = \sum_{J} (-1)^{|J|} \det_q(A_J) the alternating sum of quantum minors, which reduces to \det(I - A) at q = 1 where the MacMahon Master Theorem inverts it as \sum_n \mathrm{tr}\,S^n(A), every knot diagram K has an arc-graph matrix B'_K with J_n(K,q) = q^{\delta(K,n)} / \mathrm{Ferm}(B'_K), n-evaluated [garoufalidis-loebl2005, §1, Def. 1.4 and Thm. 2]. That theorem expresses J_n as the inverse of a non-commutative fermionic partition function; it is not a statement about Wedderburn multiplicities of H_n(q), so the identification of \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} as a partition-algebra count above is made here and is not supplied by it.

Conditional structure

The conjecture is conditional on the joint-tower SDP completeness: i.e. the joint-tower SDP solver of the canonical formalism, which does not yet exist, gives a unique non-negative integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(K_w) for every bound-state knot K_w. Until that solver is available, the identity is verified on two census atoms and extrapolated to {}^{4}\mathrm{He} with explicit caveat. The hypothesis asserts, for each atom a with volume \mathrm{Vol}(a) > 0 and with m_e > 0, a positive integer \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(a) such that \rho_F(a) = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}(a), together with the binding formula B_{\mathrm{pred}}(a) = \rho_F(a)\, m_e\, \mathrm{Vol}(a).

The quantities \rho_F, \mathrm{Vol} and m_e are given data rather than existentials, so the hypothesis is refutable: a prefactor lying strictly between two consecutive naturals — as the {}^{4}\mathrm{He} datum \rho_F \approx 1.889 does — admits no \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} at all.

The hypothesis is not established. That is the open state: establishing it would require supplying \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}}, and no operational definition in the corpus yet reproduces the confirmed 1, 2, 2. The hypothesis deliberately does not identify \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} with any SDP construction — the Wedderburn saturating projection whose dimension it is meant to be is not constructed here — so what it states is the positive-integrality of the prefactor and the binding formula it feeds, and nothing more.

Notation hazard resolved

Before the present convention, three distinct quantities used the symbol \rho in QOU compute and content (per atom-knot-mass-derivation §Notation):

  • \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} — integer Wedderburn multiplicity (this conjecture)
  • \rho_K — CODATA-fit density per knot
  • \rho_F — Kashaev prefactor in the formal derivation (unnamed, compute-only)

The present convention consolidates around the canonical \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} name, removing the third unnamed \rho.

Where \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} is used

  • the atom assignment of the binding computation, which reads \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} and emits B_{\mathrm{pred}} = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \cdot m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K)
  • atom-knot-mass-derivation §Algorithm step 3 — supplies \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} via joint-tower SDP

What remains open

  1. {}^{4}\mathrm{He} resolved (negative). The binding-arbiter probe found \rho_F(⁴\mathrm{He}) \approx 1.889 — not an integer, and no categorical count derives the cap at 2 (see §Evidence). The open successors are sharper: (a) is \rho_F even integer-valued at doubly-magic nuclei? and (b) derive the doubly-magic prefactor directly (including Coulomb), rather than rounding 1.89 \to 2. The census-knot atoms ({}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{3}\mathrm{He}) remain the exact domain of the \rho_F = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} identity; {}^{2}\mathrm{H} left that domain when its knot assignment was retired (see §Evidence).
  2. Extend joint-tower SDP to {}^{5}\mathrm{Li}, {}^{6}\mathrm{Li}, {}^{7}\mathrm{Li} — the A\in{5,6,7} gap needs \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} values; the wider atom\toknot census is deferred until the full SDP solver is available.
  3. Extend joint-tower SDP to α-cluster atoms ({}^{8}\mathrm{Be} and up) — the α-cluster rule inherits \rho_F = 2 from {}^{4}\mathrm{He}; verifying \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} = 2 across the α-cluster recursion would close the inheritance step.
